messages:
rachel: Starting an experiment I call 'ownership compartmentalization' — carve narrow runtime compartments so teams can own pieces without cross-service hacks. Not a big rip; iterative safety-first approach. Quick sync tomorrow?

omar: +1. What's first cut? session lease + local tenant metadata + eviction policy?

vikram: sounds right. main constraint: we must avoid degrading batch economics. propose a two-layer approach: compatibility facade + per-compartment batch coordinator optional.

sylvia: ops note: need placement API + lease semantics and clear rollback per-tenant. Also require per-tenant dashboards for cost and latency delta.

rachel: rollout plan: 1) implement facade accepting legacy and compartment headers 2) small internal cohort canaries by tenant-shape 3) observe for 2 weeks before wider rollout. Auto-fail gating on p95/p99 regressions.

omar: acceptance criteria: p95 delta <=5% token path, no increase in downstream telemetry schema, and per-tenant rollback <10m.

vikram: testing: migration chaos (kill comp at switch), semantic diff suite on canonical prompts, batch-size distribution checks.

sylvia: ops runbook: warm-new-compartment -> switch header -> drain old -> validate outputs. dashboards: comp.hit_rate, comp.batch_size, comp.queue_p99.

rachel: owners: omar (placement + leases), vikram (batching prototype), sylvia (ops/runbook/dashboards). I'll write a short RFC and drop link here.

deploy-bot: staging deploy scheduled; tag with "ownership-compartmentalization" and include rollback playbook link.
